elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "All results of the Support Services and any other materials prepared by TrueLink specifically for Client under this Agreement shall be the sole property of Client"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein"
"TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface" (Section 2(d) left intact)

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "To the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results or materials, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and all data provided by or on behalf of Client or its customers, brokers or borrowers"
"No jointly owned intellectual property is created under this Agreement."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: No provision addresses generic tools or know-how; only "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: Licence is limited to embedded TrueLink IP "as part of such results or materials", not a licence to deliverables (which Client owns outright)

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: express Client ownership of results/materials with an assignment, retained Client rights in Client Content, IP and borrower/loan data, an embedded-TrueLink-IP licence that is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free, no-joint-ownership language, and Section 2(d)'s reservation of TrueLink's Interface rights left untouched.

Minimality fails: the embedded-IP licence imports fallback-only rights ('worldwide' scope plus 'use, modify and sublicense'), which exceed the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence the locked preferred level requires and mix levels.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (no generic tools/know-how ownership statement and no standalone deliverables licence), but that is immaterial because the drafter's locked target is preferred.

Intent is preserved: the Credit Data licence in Section 8(d) is expressly carved out, the confidentiality carve-outs and Section 13 term/renewal mechanics are unchanged, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced (the insertion is numbered 'e' after the existing Ownership paragraph).
